Greptile Summary

 Metadata changes received from independently backed peer filers now retry transient replay failures and expose terminal failures through a peer-labelled metric and more specific logging. - Adds bounded retries around peer metadata replay. - Records retry-exhausted or non-transient replay failures. - Adds tests for transient recovery and permanent failure handling. - Documents that replaying delete-and-insert operations is non-transactional.

Confidence Score: 5/5

 The PR appears safe to merge because no blocking failure remains within the eligible follow-up-review scope. No blocking failure remains.

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | weed/filer/meta_aggregator.go | Adds synchronous bounded replay retries and surfaces terminal failures while deliberately continuing peer-stream processing. | | weed/filer/meta_aggregator_replay_test.go | Covers recovery from a transient insertion failure and observability of a permanent failure. | | weed/filer/meta_replay.go | Documents the existing non-transactional delete-and-insert replay behavior. | | weed/stats/metrics.go | Registers a peer-labelled counter for metadata replay failures. |

Sequence Diagram

 ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Peer as Peer filer participant Aggregator as Meta aggregator participant Retry as util.Retry participant Store as Local filer store participant Metrics as Metrics/logging Peer->>Aggregator: Metadata event Aggregator->>Retry: replicateMetadataChange(event) loop Replay attempts Retry->>Store: Replay(event) Store-->>Retry: success or error end alt Replay succeeds Retry-->>Aggregator: success else Retry exhausted or error is permanent Retry-->>Aggregator: terminal error Aggregator->>Metrics: "Increment replay_failures{peer}" Aggregator->>Metrics: Log diverged entry end Aggregator->>Aggregator: Continue stream and advance offset ```

body: The retry-and-surface approach looks right, and the tests verifying both the transient and permanent paths are good. I pushed a simplification commit: reused the existing stubFilerStore for the test fakes, and trimmed the comments and the third test that documented the pre-existing DeleteEntry partial-failure hazard. That hazard is real but predates this PR, and a test asserting a bug still exists would break the moment someone fixes it at the store layer. Better tracked as its own issue if it bites in practice.
